decision_reason: The assigned source is Cypress.io's privately developed browser testing framework. The French SILL listing and Pacific Northwest National Laboratory case study show public-sector recommendation/use, but neither establishes government authorship, commissioning, funding, or stewardship of this source. Government use is not government provenance.

government_provenance.note: Cypress's own history identifies this as a company-created test product; its 2017 open-source announcement describes an internal Cypress team making its existing product public. The French SILL record is an adoption/catalog lead, and PNNL's case study documents a downstream user; neither connects an agency to creation, commissioning, funding, or stewardship of this repository.

public_source.note: The canonical public monorepo provides the Cypress desktop test runner/app, CLI, browser driver and first-party packages, with direct install commands and developer documentation. The separate paid Cypress Cloud service is not this repository; no credentials are needed to read or install the public source.

eligible_license.note: The current root file is the complete OSI-approved MIT grant for first-party software and accompanying files in this repository. The vendor's 2018 statement also expressly identifies the Test Runner as MIT-licensed. Cypress Cloud is a separate commercial service and third-party dependencies retain their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: The named DOE Pacific Northwest National Laboratory case study says PNNL selected Cypress for end-to-end testing of its RedEye application and lists the Cypress App as a product used. This supports independent operational use/notability only; it is not provenance evidence. The public repository also carries installation/user documentation and current releases.

product_identity: Cypress Test Runner/Cypress App and CLI: a browser end-to-end and component testing framework in the cypress-io/cypress monorepo; excludes the separately offered Cypress Cloud service
agency: No government sponsor identified; Cypress.io is the product creator. U.S. DOE Pacific Northwest National Laboratory is a documented downstream user only.
geography: United States (private product origin; no government-sponsor geography established)
license: MIT for first-party software and accompanying files in the cypress-io/cypress repository; Cypress Cloud and third-party dependencies are outside this grant
family_note: The assigned source is the Cypress browser testing framework, not the unrelated CMS/ONC eCQM test tool also named Cypress. Repository documentation scopes the source to the test runner/app, CLI, driver and first-party packages; the paid Cypress Cloud service is separate. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: Active: the source is publicly distributed with current documentation and releases. Cypress's 2017 post says it opened the code to the public; 2018 is the first primary source located here that expressly states the Test Runner is MIT-licensed, so that is the conservative first defensible year for a specifically eligible public grant. The SILL listing and PNNL use do not establish government origin.

decision_reason: Harden-Sysvol is an independently authored security PowerShell module, not a government-created, commissioned, funded, or stewarded product. The SILL listing is a government discovery/use lead only and does not establish provenance.

government_provenance.note: The first-party repository identifies author Mehdi Dakhama and credits HardenAD community contributors; its README describes a personal project and does not identify an agency contract, government funding, sponsorship, or stewardship. SILL presence is not evidence of government authorship or funding.

public_source.note: The public repository exposes the PowerShell module source, documentation, examples and install/usage instructions without credentials; the README also links an author-published PowerShell Gallery distribution.

eligible_license.note: The repository contains the complete GNU Affero General Public License version 3 text (AGPL-3.0-only; OSI-approved). Its README explicitly says the project follows AGPLv3, citing its use of PsWritePDF/iText. This is the grant for Harden-Sysvol's first-party module source; dependencies remain under their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: The official PowerShell Gallery distributes HardenSysvol with PowerShell install instructions and version history; that page lists version 2.2.5 dated 2026-01-22. The first-party README explains supported Windows/Server environments, installation, operations and reports. This is operational distribution/notability evidence, not government provenance.

product_identity: Harden-Sysvol (HardenSysvol), a PowerShell module to audit Active Directory Group Policy and SYSVOL contents for sensitive data, misconfiguration and suspicious files
agency: No government sponsor identified; authored by individual developer Mehdi Dakhama with HardenAD community contributors
geography: No public-agency sponsor geography established; the developer's jurisdiction was not confirmed
license: AGPL-3.0-only for Harden-Sysvol first-party module source; dependencies retain their own terms
family_note: The assigned GitHub repository is the standalone module; it is also distributed as Hardensysvol through PowerShell Gallery. The root grant is AGPLv3, not a government software license. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: Active: the README was updated 2026-09-25 and PowerShell Gallery lists a 2.2.5 release on 2026-01-22. The LICENSE history feed shows the first root AGPL license commit on 2024-05-14 (commit linked above); this, not the source-screen metadata or a package date, supports 2024 as the first observed licensed-source year. Rejected for absent government provenance.

decision_reason: Dalgo is a private Project Tech4Dev product for NGOs. Its own Digital Public Goods profile says NGO partners use it in programs involving State Governments; that is downstream use, not public-sector creation, commissioning, funding, or stewardship. The assigned URL is also an organization page rather than one canonical product repository, so exact family source and grant scope remain unresolved.

government_provenance.note: The DPGA profile identifies Project Tech4Dev as owner, classifies it as Private and gives India as its origin country. It describes NGO partners talking to State Governments and partners deploying their own solutions/programs there while using Dalgo. That is third-party platform use, not government provenance for Dalgo. Tech4Dev's first-party launch page likewise identifies it as its open-source product.

public_source.note: The organization page is public and its README describes Dalgo and links code, but it is not a canonical repository. It identifies separate backend, React frontend and documentation repos and now also lists a monorepo and supporting services; the full source family corresponding to the present product has not been established from this org-root lead.

eligible_license.note: The organization README states Dalgo is AGPL-3.0 and the DPGA marks the product-level AGPL-3.0 license as verified; the public DDP_backend repo also has an AGPL-3.0 root grant. However, the assigned org URL is not a code repository and the grants/scope of all material frontend, monorepo and support components were not reconciled. Do not apply one repository's text automatically to the complete family.

primary_evidence.note: Project Tech4Dev's product launch page identifies Dalgo v1.0 as its open-source data platform and records pilots/early adopters including Dost Education, SNEHA, STiR Education, SHRI and Antarang. Its later product page and DPGA listing document NGO users and a current social-sector purpose. These establish product/use evidence but not public sponsorship.

product_identity: Dalgo, Project Tech4Dev's data-management and analytics platform for NGOs; the assigned URL is the developer organization, not a product-level code root
agency: No government product sponsor identified; privately owned/developed by Project Tech4Dev. State Governments are mentioned as downstream NGO-partner environments only.
geography: India (DPGA-listed product origin); no public-agency sponsor geography established
license: Product-level sources state AGPL-3.0, but exact grants and first licensed-source year across the material repository family remain unresolved
family_note: The DPGA submitted the GitHub organization URL as the source. The org README maps the platform to a backend, React frontend and docs; the current organization separately lists an all-services monorepo and infrastructure/support repos. The backend repository has an AGPL-3.0 grant, but that does not establish the license scope of the complete current product. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: Project Tech4Dev announced Dalgo v1.0 as open source in September 2023 and describes Dalgo 2.0 as its evolving social-sector platform. That launch date is not used as a first public licensed-source year because the assigned org URL does not identify a single canonical repo or a family-wide first grant commit. Current product/source mapping and component grant scope remain unresolved; the decisive rejection is absence of a public-agency provenance relationship.

decision_reason: The Data Observation Toolkit is a distinct DataKind/Medic public-health data-quality product co-developed with Uganda's Ministry of Health. The single public repository contains the toolkit's engine, Docker deployment and UI configuration under an explicit MIT grant. Medic's reports document Ministry co-development and training/use; DataKind reports continued use in Uganda and Lesotho in 2025, and the source itself has current 2026 activity.

government_provenance.note: Medic's 2022 annual report identifies the Data Observation Toolkit as co-developed with DataKind, BRAC Uganda, Uganda's Ministry of Health and other health partners. Medic's Q1 2023 impact report separately documents training six Uganda Ministry of Health staff to use DOT. This is product-specific government co-development/stewardship evidence, not a claim that the Ministry authored every file or paid all project costs.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the DOT application/code, Docker deployment, database models and UI configuration, as well as runnable setup and user/developer documentation. It is accessible without credentials; no material separate first-party source repository was required by the reviewed README.

eligible_license.note: LICENSE.md contains the complete MIT grant and names DataKind copyright (2022); MIT is OSI-approved. The grant is recorded for first-party code and files in this repository only; DBT, Great Expectations, Appsmith/runtime dependencies and externally hosted sample datasets remain under their own terms.

primary_evidence.note: DataKind's 2025 product-specific article says DOT is already making a difference in Uganda and Lesotho; the project repository supplies runnable Docker setup and UI/user guidance, and Medic's Uganda reports document MoH training/deployment work. This supports real-world use and notability rather than relying on the Digital Public Goods listing alone.

product_identity: Data Observation Toolkit (DOT), a configurable public-health data-quality monitoring engine with database, rules/tests, Docker deployment and web UI
agency: Uganda Ministry of Health (documented co-developer and implementation partner); DataKind, Medic, BRAC Uganda and other health organizations are development partners
geography: Uganda (documented government co-development and implementation); the toolkit is also reported in use in Lesotho
license: MIT for first-party source and documentation in DataKind/Data-Observation-Toolkit; external dependencies and linked sample data retain their own terms
family_note: The assigned canonical repository is a single DOT source family: it contains the data-quality application, Docker deployment and bundled UI configuration. DBT, Great Expectations, Appsmith and other dependencies are separate projects; linked sample data are not claimed under the source-code grant. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: Active: the public commit feed shows substantive repository commits through 2026-08-19. The first path-specific LICENSE.md commit is dated 2022-10-11 and supplies the first defensible public grant-bearing source year; the 2020 prototype date and DPG registry fields are not treated as source years. Product-specific 2025 use evidence and current source activity satisfy the freshness and notability baseline.

decision_reason: Dataport, an institution under public law owned by German Länder and a public local-authority IT association, identifies POLAR as its own reusable map component and makes the matching source public. The repository has an exact EUPL-1.2 grant, versioned npm/prebuilt releases and installation guidance; Dataport documents POLAR in current online services across its constituent states. The 2023 root-license history is the first defensible public grant year for this source.

government_provenance.note: Dataport's official Open Source page expressly calls POLAR a map component developed by Dataport and says it is published as an open-source GitHub project. Dataport's official identity page describes it as an institution under public law, a not-for-profit public-administration IT provider, and lists its state/local-authority owners. This is public-body authorship of the specific component, not inference from its account name.

public_source.note: This is the canonical public POLAR monorepo, containing its plugin-based map client source and packages. Its README and getting-started guide document npm installation, prebuilt releases, cloning/building and example clients; no login is required.

eligible_license.note: The repository root contains the full EUPL version 1.2 text and GitHub identifies the exact grant as EUPL-1.2, an OSI-approved license. This covers first-party POLAR repository code; OpenLayers/masterportalAPI, runtime libraries and other dependencies have separate terms.

primary_evidence.note: Dataport says POLAR is established in the online services of its owner states and appears in many online administrative application processes when geospatial data are needed. The repository lists concrete clients including Meldemichel Hamburg and Denkmalatlas Schleswig-Holstein and offers current versioned npm/prebuilt distributions plus setup guidance.

product_identity: POLAR (Plugins for OpenLAyeRs), Dataport's reusable plugin-based map client/library and family of configurable map packages
agency: Dataport AöR (public-law institution and public IT provider owned by six German Länder and IT-Verbund Schleswig-Holstein AöR); product developer
geography: Northern Germany: Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg, Bremen, Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania (tax administration), Lower Saxony and Saxony-Anhalt; IT-Verbund Schleswig-Holstein AöR
license: EUPL-1.2 for first-party source/packages in the Dataport/polar monorepo; third-party dependencies remain separately licensed
family_note: The assigned repository is the product-level package/client monorepo, not a separate demo or deployment instance. It includes configurable client/plugin source and packaged examples; upstream OpenLayers/masterportalAPI and dependencies remain outside the grant. No exact GOSDIR catalog match was found.
status_note: Active: GitHub's release page lists 2026 versioned npm/prebuilt releases, including @polar/polar@3.0.0-alpha.3, and the current guide documents installation. The root LICENSE path history feed contains a first/only grant-bearing commit dated 2023-11-08 (linked above), which supports the conservative 2023 source year rather than a registry/mirror creation date. Dataport's current official page documents continued government-service use.
